audience.text: Python developers building document processing applications who need to parse and convert DOCX, DOC, RTF, Markdown, and plain-text files programmatically.

capabilities.text: Reads DOCX, DOC (Word 97-2003), RTF, Markdown, and plain-text files into a shared Light Document Model using format-specific readers.
capabilities.title: Multi-format document reading

capabilities.text: Represents parsed documents as typed Pydantic models accessible via Document.light_document_model, enabling inspection and manipulation.
capabilities.title: Format-agnostic document model

capabilities.text: Exports to DOCX, Markdown, PDF, and plain text using dedicated writers and configurable save options.
capabilities.title: Multi-target export

capabilities.text: Embeds images as base64 data URIs in Markdown, renders them in PDF via ShapeRenderer, and preserves them losslessly in DOCX round-trips.
capabilities.title: Image handling

capabilities.text: Tunes Markdown, PDF, and DOCX output through MarkdownSaveOptions, PdfSaveOptions, and OoxmlSaveOptions.
capabilities.title: Configurable export options

capabilities.text: Extracts plain text from any loaded document using Document.get_text() or saves directly with SaveFormat.TEXT.
capabilities.title: Plain-text extraction

limitations.text: SaveFormat.DOC is defined for API compatibility but Document.save() does not implement a DOC writer; saving to DOC raises ValueError.
OoxmlSaveOptions.compliance set to ISO29500_2008_STRICT raises NotImplementedError; only ECMA376_2006 and ISO29500_2008_TRANSITIONAL are implemented.

Eight PdfSaveOptions fields (text_compression, embed_full_fonts, use_core_fonts, font_embedding_mode, page_mode, color_mode, preserve_form_fields, memory_optimization) are not yet consumed by the PDF writer.

problems_solved.text: Enables pure-Python document conversion across common formats (DOCX, DOC, RTF, Markdown, text) without external dependencies like Microsoft Word or COM automation.
Provides a unified Light Document Model to parse and manipulate documents regardless of input format, supporting round-trip editing and export.
Supports image-containing documents by embedding base64 data URIs in Markdown output and rendering shapes in PDF output using fpdf2.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Words FOSS for Python is a free, open-source Python library for reading and writing Word documents without Microsoft Word or COM automation.

uncertainties: Whether the library supports reading or writing ODT or other non-mentioned formats beyond DOCX/DOC/RTF/Markdown/text.
Whether the Light Document Model supports advanced features like macros, VBA projects, or digital signatures.
Whether the PDF writer supports form fields or interactive elements beyond static rendering.
Whether the library supports document encryption or password-protected input files.
Whether the library supports document comparison, revision tracking, or merge operations.
Whether the library supports HTML input or output beyond Markdown.
Whether the library supports streaming large documents without loading entirely into memory.
Whether the library supports custom font substitution or font embedding beyond fpdf2's capabilities.

workflows.name: Load and convert document
workflows.text: Construct a Document from a file path, then call save() with a SaveFormat constant or save options to export to DOCX, Markdown, PDF, or plain text.

workflows.name: Parse Markdown with structure
workflows.text: Load Markdown files using MarkdownLoadOptions to parse headings, lists, emphasis, tables, and embedded images as typed document nodes.

workflows.name: Export to PDF with built-in renderer
workflows.text: Use LdmPdfWriter backed by fpdf2 to render paragraphs, tables, and shapes to PDF without external engines or system fonts.

workflows.name: Round-trip DOCX editing
workflows.text: Load a DOCX file, modify the Light Document Model, and write it back using LdmDocxWriter to preserve headers, footers, images, and styles.
